name: Ink-Grinding Breath (Ma Mặc Tức)
concept: The apprentice grinds the pine-soot ink stick on a wet stone for an hour each morning, and breathes with the stroke: Wood qi from the soot or Water qi from the stone, whichever the root takes. It is a patient method that teaches the hand to be steady. In a fight it lays ink on the holder's blade or fist; an ink-marked foe is slowed.
lore: The founder Kỷ Thu Tịch's rule: no brush is touched before a thousand mornings of grinding.

name: Painted Dipper Canon (Họa Đẩu Kinh)
concept: The talisman method of the Hall. The cultivator paints the seven stars of the Dipper on their own meridians in qi, one star a layer, and draws on them to charge a talisman with one stroke. In a fight the holder throws Dipper talismans: each star painted in sequence strengthens the next, and the seventh completes the figure.
lore: Written by the founder after she watched the Pivot's watchmen on Trích Tinh Phong (A084) and painted what they saw. The Pivot buys its Dipper talismans from the Hall; its own disciples cannot paint them.

name: Rain-Fast Ink Art (Vũ Bất Hóa Mặc Pháp)

effects.name: Rainfast Ink (Vũ Bất Thoát)
effects.rule: A passive art (authored wish d35). Your talisman marks, and the debuff stacks and curses your talismans lay, cannot be cleansed; a cleanse that would remove them removes nothing of yours.

concept: The Hall's secret: the painter binds the ink to the paper with their own Water qi, so that water cannot loosen what Water holds. Talismans painted by it do not run in rain, river or blood (V059). In a fight the holder's talismans last longer and cannot be washed off by a foe's cleansing.
lore: The Hall says the founder found it by painting in the rain for a year. The truth is in the sealed book: it is the blood-ink writ of Thorn and Ink Verses, with the blood taken out and the painter's Water put in.
